issues.legal_issue: Claimants in acquisition proceedings pending when the relevant compensation amendments applied are entitled to the amended compensation benefits.
material_facts: Land was acquired for a public housing scheme under the housing authority’s enabling law.
The claimants’ acquisition proceedings were pending in 1984.
The claimants challenged the compensation awarded for their land.
issues.conclusion: The claimants were entitled to solatium at 30%, interest and additional compensation under the Land Acquisition (Amendment) Act, 1984.
issues.legal_principle: Following Savitri Cairae v. U.P. Avas Evam Vikas Parishad, the claimants were entitled to the benefits of the Land Acquisition (Amendment) Act, 1984. The Court also referred to U.P. Avas Evam Vikas Parishad v. Jainul Islam in framing the issue.

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_appeal: The claimant challenged the compensation awarded for land acquired by a public authority.
predicates.acquisition_proceedings_pending_when_ame: The acquisition proceedings remained pending when the relevant compensation amendments applied.

issues.definition: When a claimant challenges compensation in an acquisition appeal and the proceedings were pending when the amendments applied, amended compensation benefits are awarded.

issues.legal_issue: Separate compensation is payable for land and improvements when their values were separately assessed and were not capitalised together.
material_facts: The land acquisition officer assessed compensation separately for the land, structures and tube wells.
The land and improvement values were not capitalised together.
The High Court denied separate compensation for the structures and tube wells.
issues.conclusion: The claimants were entitled to separate compensation for the land, structures and tube wells.
issues.legal_principle: The Court distinguished Ratan Kumar Tandon v. State of U.P., where land and structure values had been capitalised together. Separate compensation was appropriate here because there had been no such capitalisation and the land acquisition officer had assessed the items separately.

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_appeal: The claimant challenged compensation in proceedings concerning acquired land.
predicates.improvements_separately_assessed: The land acquisition officer separately assessed compensation for improvements on the land.
predicates.land_and_improvements_capitalised_togeth: The value of the land and improvements was combined through capitalisation.

issues.definition: In an acquisition compensation appeal, separate assessment without combined capitalisation supports separate compensation for the land and its improvements.

issues.legal_issue: The deduction for development costs must reflect the development required in the particular acquisition rather than a fixed general rate.
material_facts: The acquiring authority challenged the deduction made for development costs.
The acquired tract comprised about 27 acres.
The Court considered that development costs varied according to the location, area and work required.
issues.conclusion: The Court increased the development-cost deduction from 10% to 25%.
issues.legal_principle: There is no fixed deduction for development costs: the appropriate deduction varies from place to place and according to the area and the development work required. The Court relied on that principle and considered the size of the acquired tract in fixing the deduction.

predicates.acquiring_authority_appeals_development_: The acquiring authority appealed the deduction applied to account for development costs.
predicates.development_costs_required: Development work was required for the acquired land.
predicates.existing_deduction_inadequate: The Court found that the deduction already applied did not adequately account for development costs.

issues.definition: When an acquiring authority challenges a development-cost deduction, development is required, and the existing deduction is inadequate, the deduction is increased.
